claim: FDA approved donor-islet therapy for a narrow adult T1D population with recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
population_or_model: Adults with T1D and recurrent severe hypoglycemia
design: Regulatory approval and supporting clinical studies
endpoint: FDA indication; glycemic control and severe hypoglycemia
limitations: Narrow selected indication; donor supply, invasive procedure, immunosuppression risks; not general cure
notes: Use label and primary reports for exact efficacy denominator and adverse-event rates

claim: In the phase 1-2 zimislecel study, 10 of 12 full-dose recipients were insulin-independent at day 365
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
analysis_denominator: 10/12 full-dose recipients; 14 participants had at least 12 months follow-up across parts
limitations: Small and short-term; selected cohort; insulin independence does not establish cure or freedom from immunosuppression

claim: Neutropenia was the most common serious adverse event in the zimislecel study and occurred in three participants
population_or_model: People with T1D in phase 1-2 study
limitations: Small cohort; do not infer causality beyond the authors' attribution
notes: The paper describes neutropenia as the most common serious adverse event

claim: Two deaths occurred during zimislecel study follow-up: cryptococcal meningitis and progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment
population_or_model: People with T1D in phase 1-2 study
limitations: Authors reported no serious adverse events considered related or possibly related to zimislecel; causes reported were cryptococcal meningitis and progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment
notes: Report events and the study's causality assessment separately

claim: At 14 months, a single recipient of gene-edited donor islets had continued graft function without immunosuppression; insulin independence was not demonstrated
cointerventions: Gene-edited allogeneic islets; no immunosuppressive drugs
limitations: One participant; exploratory endpoint; continued graft function does not establish insulin independence, efficacy, or population safety
notes: The 2026 NEJM report follows the same recipient reported in 2025

claim: Vertex reported that VX-264 did not meet its efficacy endpoint in phase 1-2 and would not advance further in clinical development
population_or_model: People with T1D in the VX-264 phase 1-2 study
analysis_denominator: Not reported in the cited sponsor update; underlying phase 1/2 enrollment should be added from the official record or trial report
cointerventions: Encapsulated allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; device intended to avoid immunosuppression
limitations: Sponsor announcement; it does not establish the biological reason for insufficient efficacy
notes: Company said additional analyses were planned; mechanism of failure remains unresolved from these sources

claim: FDA accelerated approval allows teplizumab to delay decline in endogenous insulin production in certain 8-17 year-olds with recently diagnosed stage 3 T1D
population_or_model: Pediatric patients age 8-17 with recent stage 3 T1D
design: Adequate and well-controlled trial; accelerated approval
analysis_denominator: Regulatory claim; participant analysis denominator to be added from trial publication
endpoint: C-peptide surrogate endpoint; postapproval study required
limitations: Delay/preservation is not cure; surrogate endpoint; boxed warning for viral reactivation
